payload.logline: A small girl on a balcony waits every evening for her dad's car, and the headlights that finally turn into the street bring something even better.
payload.change: Mia goes from waiting to celebrating, but not for the reason she expected.

structure.name: kishotenketsu
structure.why: Four parts with a twist and no villain fit a 15 to 20 second film and a gentle joke. Considered setup-and-punchline (too thin on character) and man in a hole (too long for 20 seconds).

structureBeats.name: ki
structureBeats.summary: Evening; Mia on tiptoe at the balcony rail, watching the street.

structureBeats.name: sho
structureBeats.summary: She knows what she is waiting for: Dad's car.

structureBeats.name: ten
structureBeats.summary: Headlights turn the corner. It is not Dad. It is a pizza scooter.

characters.obstacle: None; the twist supplies the turn.
characters.visibleTrait: Always on tiptoe, chin barely over the rail.

setting.location: Third-floor apartment balcony over a quiet residential street
setting.timeOfDay: blue hour, just after the streetlights come on
setting.light: Warm lamp light from the window behind Mia; cool blue street; one streetlight on the corner
details: A street corner with a single streetlight

tone.humour: Reversal of expectation, landed by an understated last line

styleProfile.framing: Balanced, generous negative space; child's eye height for her shots
styleProfile.angles: Low from the street for the establishing shot, eye level at child height, high-angle point of view
styleProfile.lens: Normal; long for the point of view down the street
styleProfile.movement: Holds with gentle parallax drifts and push-ins only
styleProfile.key: Mid-low key; warm practical light against cool blue
styleProfile.editing: Unhurried; the longest hold on the final image

payload.audience: General, all ages; short vertical video
payload.synopsis: Six o'clock, blue hour. Mia, on tiptoe at her balcony rail, keeps watch over the street the way she does every evening, waiting for the sound of Dad's car. Headlights swing round the corner and she leans out, certain. It isn't Dad: it's a pizza scooter, turning towards her building. Mia throws both arms in the air. Even better.
